extra.message: Password-reset token exposed in response and log file — Account takeover of any user by obtaining their reset token from the response/log. [verified: request_password_reset always writes the plaintext reset token to local_mocks/password_resets.log (line ~507) and returns it as dev_reset_token in the HTTP response whenever APP_ENV != 'production' (line ~513); confirm_password_reset accepts that token directly, so obtaining it via the response or log grants account takeover bypassing email ownership.]

No brute-force protection / rate limiting on login — Attackers can run unlimited online password-guessing and credential-stuffing against any account, including ops_admin, leading to account takeover. [verified: The /api/auth/login handler only does an email lookup plus verify_password with no attempt counter, lockout, delay, or rate-limiting, and no throttling middleware/library exists anywhere in the app, enabling unlimited online password guessing.]

CSV formula injection in exported reports — Formula execution / data exfiltration on the export recipient's spreadsheet client. [verified: csv_response writes user-controllable fields (customer company_name, incident customer_summary/internal_notes/resolution, addresses) via csv.DictWriter.writerow (line ~1382) with no neutralization of leading =,+,-,@, so cells can execute as formulas when opened in a spreadsheet client.]

CSV formula injection in route schedule export — Formula injection in route-schedules.csv; opening the export in Excel/Sheets can execute attacker-supplied formulas, enabling data exfiltration or command execution on the analyst's machine. [verified: export_routes writes user-controllable fields (job.customer.company_name, job.location.address_line1, worker.user.full_name) into CSV via csv_response, which uses csv.DictWriter with no neutralization of leading =,+,-,@ formula characters.]

CSV formula injection in incident export — A low-privilege customer can plant a spreadsheet formula in customer_summary that executes when staff open incidents.csv, enabling data theft or command execution on the staff workstation. [verified: A low-privilege customer can create an incident with arbitrary customer_summary (only length-validated in schemas.IncidentIn), which export_incidents writes verbatim into incidents.csv via csv_response with no formula-character escaping.]

Account enumeration via registration response — Attacker can enumerate which email addresses have accounts to target them. [verified: register raises HTTP 409 'An account with this email already exists' for taken emails (line ~454) versus a 200 success for new ones, and there is no rate limiting on register/login/reset, allowing reliable account enumeration.]

Session cookie set without Secure flag on registration — Session cookie can be sniffed over HTTP, enabling session hijacking. [verified: The /api/auth/register handler hardcodes secure=False on response.set_cookie (line ~493) while /api/auth/login uses secure=os.getenv('COOKIE_SECURE',...) (line ~428), so the registration session cookie ignores the COOKIE_SECURE config and can be sent over plaintext HTTP; impact is low since the env default is already false.]

No rate limiting on password-reset request endpoint — Unthrottled password-reset requests enable abuse/DoS and assist account enumeration against the reset flow. [verified: request_password_reset has no rate limiting, branches on user existence (only acts when user exists and is not disabled), and returns dev_reset_token when APP_ENV!=production, enabling unthrottled abuse and account-enumeration assistance.]
